Joint-Standing Committee on Education & Cultural Affairs
Testimony in Support of LD 1558, "Resolve, Establishing the Commission to Update Maine's Public Policy on Higher Education"
Thursday, April 24, 2025
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and distinguished members of the Joint-Standing Committee on Education & Cultural Affairs, my name is Chace Jackson, and I serve as Maine Maritime Academy's Legislative Affairs Coordinator. Today I am expressing our support for LD 1558, "Resolve Establishing the Commission to Update Maine's Public Policy on Higher Education". As suggested by its title this bill would establish a Commission with a diverse range of stakeholders to assess challenges in Maine's higher education environment. We would also like to thank Rep. Sargent for her leadership in fostering this discussion.
Established in 1941 and based in Castine, MMA is Maine's special-purpose college and in fact one of only six State Maritime Academies founded to play a vital role in our nation's maritime interests and national security. We bridge this state's proud seafaring tradition with its storied role in American maritime history, training Maine students who become the finest mariners operating vessels all around the globe. In addition, we offer degrees in the fields of engineering, marine transportation, marine biology and oceanography, and international business and logistics. Our graduates are commonly recognized by industry employers as the best among all maritime academies. Many of our students are members of our Regiment of Midshipmen which is a rigorous course of military-style training, discipline and leadership. MMA prides itself as "Maine's Leadership College".
Our support of LD 1558 is meant to remain consistent with our enthusiastic support for LD 681, "An Act Regarding Public Higher Education Funding in the State". Sponsored by Sen. Grohoski with Rep. Foster as lead-cosponsor, LD 681 is our greatest priority for the 132nd Legislature. The only caveat to our support for LD 1558 today is our hope that one bill not detract from the other. The second and lesser portion of LD 681 creates a similar working group to the Commission suggested by LD 1558. We think it is important that work move forward following the 1st Regular Session no matter the vehicle. We are encouraged to see the legislature acting creatively to address a broad spectrum of higher education challenges before the state and believe public higher education funding should loom large among them.

To recap, LD 681 is about aligning Maine Maritime Academy's public funding with that of other higher education institutions in Maine and, more critically, with the nation's other State Maritime Academies (SMAs). Currently, Maine Maritime Academy is Maine's most expensive public higher education institution--an unfortunate distinction it also holds among SMAs. This funding disparity has made it harder for MMA to attract and retain students, especially when other maritime academies are more cost-competitive for Maine residents. LD 681 would incrementally bring us into funding alignment with other public higher education institutions in Maine, but more importantly closer to the nation's other SMAs. Because tuition alternatives at other SMAs are significantly less, Maine resident students often choose other SMAs over Maine Maritime Academy.
Despite these financial challenges, MMA continues to lead through innovation, collaboration, and investment. And to ensure long term sustainability and competitiveness while we work to increase our operational base, Maine Maritime Academy continues to collaborate with alumni, several industries, and the federal government to aggressively add new educational programs.
As such, we believe it is important that public higher education funding is increased within this legislative session and that a Commission like the one prescribed by either of these bills moves forward to discuss sustaining funding for Maine's public higher education institutions.
MMA's only other suggestion would be that a trustee from each of the three public higher education institutions, selected by each board, be added to LD 1558's Commission. These are important voices for helping the collective group understand the challenges faced by their systems, including long-term, sustainable funding.
We would like to once again thank Rep. Sargent and the Committee for their leadership and attention to these issues. We look forward to ongoing discussions with you around public higher education funding. Thank you for your time and consideration.

PRETI FLAHERTY April 29, 2025 Page 2 LD 1285 establishes the Commission to Update Maine's Public Policy on Higher Education to review all related laws and rules addressing the State's public policy on higher education and make recommendations for potential legislative changes. The Commission shall, among its duties, analyze how best to continue to expand access to affordable high-quality higher education to help students achieve postsecondary success and prepare for the future. Testimony of Rep. Holly T. Sargent introducing
LD 1558, Resolve, Establishing the Commission to Update Maine's Public Policy on

Higher Education

Before the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs

Chair Rafferty, Chair Murphy, and fellow members of the Education and Cultural Affairs Committee,
my name is Holly Sargent, and I represent House District 147, the town of York. I am here today to
introduce LD 1558, which proposes the establishment of a commission to review Maine's laws and rules
addressing public policy on higher education.
This resolve is almost identical to a measure introduced and passed in the 1315` Legislature.

It is both timely and necessary. The Maine Revised Statutes Title 20-A, Sections 10001-13000 which govern our state's public policy on post-secondary education, have not been updated in over 20 years. In that time, significant changes have occurred--both in the higher education landscape and in the needs of
students, families and the workforce. These shifts call for a review of the laws that shape how we
approach higher education in Maine.

The proposed commission will examine existing statutes and provide recommendations for proposed changes as necessary. It will also review current funding levels and procedures for allocation and
distribution to UMS, MCCS, and MMA. It has broad representation of stakeholders and experts and is
required to report back to this committee in December of 2025.
At this time of challenge for all higher education, it is critical that Maine's relevant laws support ongoing excellence, affordability and alignment with workforce needs for its institutions. Maine's public and private colleges and universities are economic engines for growth and beacons of leaming and
opportunity.
We must ensure that our laws evolve with the times and continue to serve the best interests of Maine's
students and communities.
I urge this Committee to support LD 1558, as it represents an important step forward in creating a more
dynamic and responsive higher education system in Maine. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs Becky Smith, Director of Government and Community Relations Testimony in support of LD 1558 Resolve, Establishing the Commission to Update Maine's Public Policy on Higher Education April 24, 2025

Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs, My name is Becky Smith, and I am here today to testify in please support of LD 1558, Resolve, Establishing the Commission to Update Maine's Public Policy on Higher Education on behalf of the Maine Community College System with what I hope is a friendly amendment.
We would recommend adding a member to the proposed commission representing the Maine Community College System Board of Trustees to add some additional expertise to the commission in order to best inform the commission's outcomes. Our board members set policies for the system and are well positioned to bring considerable depth and breadth of knowledge and expertise to the commission in its work. For example, the board is actively engaged in ongoing review of programs, finances, student-related issues and both short- and long-term planning for the colleges. This commission is likely to take up a very wide range of issues, and a trustee representative will be an important voice in those discussions.
We also respectfully request that the Resolve allow the MCCS Board of Trustees to choose from its ranks to be a member of the proposed commission.
We are first and foremost an educational institution. As such we are deeply invested in Maine's public policies on higher education, their rigorous review, and the ongoing analysis of where new policies are needed to support the MCCS mission - in statute - of developing "an educated, skilled and adaptable labor force that is responsive to the changing needs of the Maine economy."
That mission and the need to be "responsive to the changing needs" of the Maine economy supports the need to have a trustee represented on the proposed commission.
We welcome the opportunity to work with our colleagues at other public higher education institutions and the legislature to review laws and rules addressing the state's public policy on higher education and make recommendations for potential legislative changes.

We respectfully recommend that you support this Resolve and support adding a member to the commission to represent the Maine Community College System Board of Trustees.

University of Maine System Testimony in Support
of LD 1558, Resolve, Establishing the Commission to Update Maine's Public Policy
on Higher Education -- Presented by UMS Chief External & Governmental Affairs
Officer Samantha Warren ---- April 24, 2025
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and distinguished members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Education & Cultural Affairs: My name is Sam Warren and l am the Chief External & Governmental Affairs Officer for the University of Maine System (UMS), which
supports LD 1558, Resolve, Establishing the Commission to Update Maine's Public Po/icy
on Higher Education.
Maine's public universities recognize that State statute governing higher education is often
outdated and does not always reflect today's postsecondary students; the new modalities in
which our institutions provide high-quality education and research learning experiences to them; and the dynamic context of higher education, employer and community need, and
innovation that leads to new and effective models of higher education. Portions of the section on public policy have not been updated since 1981, eight years before the University of Maine at Augusta (UMA) led the nation in pioneering the use of lTV to allow
place-bound learners to access higher education. And the chapter governing New Ventures
Maine, a program of our System administered by UMA, still includes language about "displaced homemakers."
Maine is unique in not having a State agency or overarching governing body strategically focused on higher education beyond the review of requests for degree-granting authority and assessment and approval of educator preparation programs (State Board of
Education). For example, in New England, New Hampshire has a Higher Education
Commission, Massachusetts has a Department of Higher Education, Vermont has a Higher Education Council, Connecticut has an Office of Higher Education, and Rhode Island has an Office of the Postsecondary Commissioner.
As the foremost educational and research enterprise in the state, UMS often takes the lead
as convenor and authority on statewide higher education matters and continues to welcome
that important responsibility. For example, the State Higher Education Executive Officer
(SHEEO) for the state is the UMS Chancellor. Additionally, at the onset of the COVID-19
pandemic, Chancellor Malloy convened the leaders of Maine's public and private institutions to develop a reopening framework, drawing on theexpertise of the University of Maine's
scientists and economists. UMS, along with our partners at the Maine Community College System (MCCS), is also a founding partner of MaineSpark, a coalition working to advance
the state's postsecondary degree/credential attainment goal, which is codified in a section of State statute focused on labor and industry (Title 26).
University of Maine - University of Maine at Augusta ' University of Maine at Farmington - University of Maine at Fort Kent University of Maine at Machias ~ University of Maine at Presque Isle - University of Southern Maine - University of Maine School of Law

Recent conversations in this Committee about the impact on Maine's higher education marketplace of public investment to advance universal college access and affordability at
only some institutions reinforce that the time is right for strategic conversation about public policy on higher education. So too does this Committee's consideration of funding fairness among public institutions that have varying levels of statewide responsibility and impact.
For these reasons, we appreciate Representative Sargent reintroducing the Resolve to create this Commission, which was unanimously endorsed by the Committee in 2023 (LD 1264), yet never convened. Not only does LD 1558 offer a long-overdue opportunity to
modernize Maine statute to reflect changes in the higher education landscape and best
practice over the past three-plus decades, but UMS hopes that it will also elevate the
increasingly important role of affordable higher education to advancing the upward mobility of Maine people and the prosperity of our state.
Regarding the composition of the Commission, UMS suggests that a member from each of
the public Boards of Trustees (UMS, MCCS, and Maine Maritime Academy) be included,
given their statutory roles in governance, policy, and planning. For UMS Trustees, this
includes responsibility to "Plan strategies for programs and allocation of resources that most effectively serve the educational needs of the citizens of this State" and "Develop and maintain a strong system of accountability to the public for performance results of the
system" -- both of which are highly relevant to the duties of the proposed Commission.
We look fon/vard to participating in this process and thank the Committee for your support of
Maine's public institutions and the more than 46,000 students we collectively enroll.
